guides.title: No sound from the speakers
guides.summary: The radio or music shows as playing, but nothing comes out, or some speakers are silent.
symptoms: music system awaaz nahi aa rahi

steps.text: Turn the volume up and look for a mute symbol on the screen.
steps.detail: In many cars, pressing the volume knob or a steering wheel button mutes the sound.

steps.text: Press Source or Media and pick the source you want: Radio, Bluetooth or USB.
Is the sound missing from all speakers or only some?
Switch the car off, lock it, wait 5 minutes and start again.
Open the sound settings and set balance and fader to the centre.
steps.detail: When balance or fader is turned fully to one side, the other speakers go quiet.

escalate.text: A speaker, its wiring or the amplifier may need a check.
tell_service: Whether it's every source or only one
When it started: after an accessory was fitted, battery work or a car wash

guides.title: Bluetooth music won't play or keeps skipping
guides.summary: Songs from the phone don't play in the car, stutter, or the song name doesn't show.
symptoms: spotify not playing in the car
gaana nahi chal raha bluetooth pe
song name not showing on the screen

steps.text: Choose Bluetooth audio as the source in the car, then press play once on the phone.
On the phone, open the car's Bluetooth settings and allow media audio.
Close other apps that play sound (videos, games), and check the sound isn't going to earbuds or a watch.
If songs skip, download them for offline play.
steps.detail: Streaming stutters when the mobile signal drops, which happens a lot on highways and in tunnels.

steps.text: Restart the phone, and restart the car's system: car off, locked, wait 5 minutes.

escalate.text: The car's media system may need a software update.
tell_service: Whether it happens with another phone
Your phone model and software version

guides.title: USB music or phone not detected
guides.summary: A pen drive isn't read, or the phone doesn't charge or play through USB.
symptoms: phone not charging in the car
pendrive ke gaane nahi chal rahe
car doesn't read my usb stick

steps.detail: Some ports only charge; usually only one carries music and data.

steps.text: Use a short data cable in good condition, or try a different one.
steps.detail: Many cheap cables can only charge.

steps.text: Is it a pen drive or a phone?
Try a smaller pen drive formatted as FAT32 with a few MP3 files.
steps.detail: Many cars only read FAT32 drives up to 32 GB and common formats such as MP3, AAC or WMA. Your owner's manual lists what your car reads.

steps.text: Unlock the phone and allow the connection when asked (Android: 'File transfer' or 'Android Auto'; iPhone: 'Trust').
Look for lint in the phone's charging port and remove it gently with a wooden toothpick, never metal.

escalate.text: The USB port or its wiring may need a check.
tell_service: Whether the port charges but doesn't play, or does nothing
